takeaways: Rate-hike fears are back: core inflation ran 3.7% annualized, a December hike looks near-certain, and the 10-year is around 5%, so CBRE sees cap rates rising 40-60 bps.
Capital is shifting to alternative lenders (48% of non-agency closings) as banks and CMBS retreat, even with Q3 sales at a four-year high of $143B.
AI risk is spreading beyond data centers: Nvidia lost ~$200B in a day on a governance scandal, while Anthropic's IPO and OpenAI's $10B quarter test investor appetite.

items.headline: Core inflation runs 3.7% annualized, making a December Fed hike near-certain and a longer cycle likely
items.summary: Core prices rose at a 3.7% annualized pace over three months through October, a third straight firm month. WSJ says the debate is now how far and how fast the Fed goes, and the 10-year Treasury was already at 5.02% on Oct 28 (via WSJ 10-Point, CRE Daily).

items.headline: Slok sees Fed needing ~275 bps more, to 6.75% by end-2027; Pensford argues an AI unwind could stop hikes
items.summary: The two views bracket the rate path that will drive CRE and senior housing refinancing costs. CBRE already sees cap rates rising 40-60 bps as the 10-year nears 5% (via The Promote, CRE Daily).

items.headline: CBRE Q3: volume $257.8B (+98%, +18% ex-entity deals) as alternative lenders take 48% of closings
items.summary: Alternative lenders rose from 37% to 48% of non-agency closings while banks fell to 26% and CMBS to 6%. Cap rates were 6.0%, DSCR eased to 1.32 and 82.3% of loans were interest-only or partial IO.

items.headline: One Beverly Hills capital stack: $4.3B construction debt from JPM and VICI, and $3B+ from Eldridge's Security Benefit
items.summary: The project grew from $5B to $10B. Security Benefit has $1.6B in loans to Eldridge entities plus $1.4B in project debt, about 4.5% of its assets, raising affiliated-lending questions (via The Promote).

items.headline: Nvidia loses ~$200B in a day amid inquiry into Jensen Huang's relationship; governance gaps exposed
items.summary: Authorities are probing a Megaspeed executive for suspected illegal chip diversion to China. Nvidia has no chairman or succession plan (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Q3 investment sales hit $143B, a four-year Q3 high, but Avison Young cuts 2026 forecast to $520B
items.summary: YTD volume is $389.3B (+17.9%), MSCI prices rose 0.9% YoY, and multifamily values fell 4.6% annually despite $119.6B in sales. The forecast cut cites renewed Fed hike concerns (via CRE Daily).

items.headline: Blackstone real estate exodus: nearly a third of senior MDs gone in three years
items.summary: BREP IX has returned 3% annualized net, and BREIT trails the 11.5% promised to the University of California (via The Promote, WSJ).

items.headline: Seven Equity plans to raze San Francisco Centre; CBRE marketing $99M bridge loan
items.summary: Ray Falack won the shuttered 1.2M sf mall at $133M and plans up to 2.4M sf of mixed-use on six acres; the deal has not closed (via The Promote).

items.headline: Brookfield walks away from a $600M downtown L.A. luxury tower
items.summary: Promote commentary reads the exit as DTLA weakness more than rates (via The Promote, WSJ).

items.headline: OpenAI Q3 revenue up ~50% to $10B but losses stay heavy; CoreWeave finds capital workaround
items.summary: CoreWeave's growth still depends on expanding data centers while cutting cost of capital, both harder now (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Anthropic founders to sell $250M each in IPO targeting ~$1.3T valuation
items.summary: Each of seven founders would retain stakes worth about $18B; the listing is slated for next week (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Data-center moratoria spread after midterms: 40+ local measures, Texas calls for freeze
items.summary: All but one restrictive ballot measure passed; about 13 GW of Texas capacity is exposed, with hundreds of billions in financing at risk (via The Promote, Nov 6).

items.headline: Furniture maker TOV tried to reinshore; tariffs made it hard
items.summary: A $100M+/yr business built on $900 sofas struggled with shifting U.S. trade policy, a small-business supply-chain lesson (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: High beef prices are here to stay as the U.S. herd hits a 75-year low
items.summary: Rebuilding takes years, so record steak and hamburger prices could last into the next decade, a food-cost headwind for operators (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Brookdale Q3: occupancy 83.1% (+130 bps) but guidance cut and stock falls ~17%
items.summary: Adjusted EBITDA rose 12% to $124.3M and RevPAR grew 7.5%, but full-year EBITDA guidance fell to $495-502M from $502-516M on marketing spend and occupancy carryover. Brookdale bought 17 leased communities for $157.4M and agreed to buy 30 more for $290M.

items.headline: Janus Living doubles portfolio to 74 properties on $2.9B of 2026 acquisitions
items.summary: Average cost is about $350K per unit at 86-87% occupancy, and 80% of deals involve no operator change. Janus has 13 operators, a $1.25B credit facility, $82M under contract for Q4, and Q3 FFO up 46% to 25 cents per share.

items.headline: American Healthcare REIT buys two California senior communities for $197M
items.summary: The 545-unit Avella at Roseville ($94.1M) and Avella at Almaden ($102.8M) came from an Affinius/Alliance JV. Senior housing sales reached about $33.3B over 12 months, up 83%, and occupancy rose for a 20th straight quarter to 89.9% (Q2 NIC MAP).

items.headline: 20-somethings ditch entry-level jobs to become their own bosses
items.summary: At least 23% of Americans aged 18-34 ran a business or side hustle last year, up from 19% in 2021 (Babson), with AI helping bypass corporate ladders (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Blackstone's Safe Harbor to buy MarineMax for $1.5B cash at $53/share, a 96% premium
items.summary: The all-cash deal (announced Aug 10) follows a competitive strategic review and is expected to close before year-end, pending shareholder and regulatory approval. MarineMax has ~70 dealerships and 65 marina/storage sites, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 7% to $611.3M even as gross margin rose to 35.7%. Infrastructure capital is paying up for recurring-revenue marinas while boat retail stays weak.

items.headline: BizBuySell Q3: 2,132 small businesses sold, median price $350K (+17% YoY)
items.summary: Closed deals were down 7% YoY, but median cash flow rose 5% to $156K. Deals above $1M averaged 3.73x cash flow and sold at 100.8% of ask, versus 2.30x and 93.6% below $1M. Service businesses were 47% of deals; restaurants fell 23%. New SBA rules took effect Oct 1.

items.headline: Acquisition entrepreneurship goes mainstream as owners retire
items.summary: A 2026 JPMorgan Chase survey found 40% of small business owners plan to retire within a decade, and about 70% have no formal or only early succession plans. Search funds, SBA loans and personal capital are financing buyers, with HVAC, accounting, home services and B2B services the common targets. Founder dependency is the key diligence risk (Forbes, May 2026).

items.headline: $26M cyberheist hits Cranbury, N.J.: wired to wrong account for a land purchase
items.summary: Police expect to recover $17.3M, leaving nearly $9M unaccounted for. A wire-verification cautionary tale for any treasury team (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Wall Street pay set to climb about 4% this year
items.summary: Options Group expects higher compensation on volatility and IPOs after last year's record $246,900 average bonus (via WSJ 10-Point).

items.headline: Exxon takes first step toward investing in Venezuela
items.summary: A preliminary deal could mark a return nearly two decades after its exit (via WSJ 10-Point).
